sourceRef: spec-sockets.md 3/4/5/6/8/10/11 + ssot-sockets.md 4.1/4.2/4.4/4.7 (module 16, `sockets`). OWNED BY MODULE 16 FROM v2 ONWARDS. v1 was forward-seeded by module 6 (base-types, build order 6) with the socketCeiling table alone, because module 6 needed the ceiling to validate the shipped 740-entry corpus and module 16 had not built yet. Module 16 has now taken ownership: the fifteen ceiling rows are UNCHANGED value for value (they are spec-sockets.md 3's own re-issued table and re-deriving them would have been a second source of truth), and every other section below is new here.
socketCeilingNote: A ROLE property. `standard` is deliberately ABSENT, not zero -- D14 puts the commander slot out of item scope entirely, and a zero row would read as 'in scope, allowed no sockets'. A base type may declare its OWN socketMax anywhere in [0, its role's ceiling]; that variation is ordinary base-type variety (module 6 measured it 740 times across the shipped corpus) and only EXCEEDING the ceiling is a violation. spec-sockets.md 3's stronger wording -- 'fixed per role, never varied per base type' -- is contradicted by the shipped corpus and is corrected here rather than enforced.
structuralCeilingNote: STRUCTURAL, exempt from AGENTS.md's no-hard-ceilings rule and required to say so. It is a LEGIBILITY limit on one item's recipe shape -- a four-ingredient recipe is memorable, a six-ingredient one is a wiki lookup -- not a ceiling on how strong an item, an insert or a combination may become. Every power axis the socket layer touches stays open: insertTiers.count is a soft content axis (raise it and the ladder extends), a combination's granted tier is unbounded above, and magnitude growth rides contentScale, which this layer never reads. Mirrored as SocketLimits.SocketMaxCeiling; the parser REFUSES a ceiling row above it rather than clamping.
maxCombosPerActorNote: A per-actor backstop on Strains and Splices (spec-sockets.md 4). NON-BINDING TODAY and honest about it: D20 fixes a Strain/Splice at 4 ingredients, so only a role whose ceiling is 4 can host one -- `armament-primary` and `core-guard` -- which makes the GEOMETRIC ceiling 2, below this 3. It is shipped so that a later widening of the 4-ceiling set cannot silently reopen the gap. Exceeding it never refuses an insert: the lowest-priority combination simply does not fire, because a tuning value must never become a player-facing wall.
rarityGrantNote: The decided shape of the `socket_min` / `socket_max` rarity_budget keys (ssot-rarity.md 5 recorded both as 'awaiting I4'): TWO INTEGERS PER RUNG, the inclusive window the socket count is rolled from at drop, before the base type's own socketMax clamps it. Transcribed from ssot-sockets.md 4.1's five ORDINAL BANDS onto the shipped ten rungs two rungs per band, not re-derived. Adjacent windows OVERLAP by design (OD4): a [1..3] item rolling 3 out-sockets a [2..4] item rolling 2, so socket count never becomes a strict ladder. APPEND-ONLY in the same sense `ordinal` is -- the count derives from the rung row at the instance's recorded catalog_revision, so a silent edit re-sockets every item ever dropped at that rung. The parser refuses a non-overlapping, non-monotonic or ceiling-breaking table at LOAD.
socketAllowanceByKindNote: species-gear-chain T4 (spec-socket-allowance-by-kind): the allowance is a property of WHAT KIND of item something is, shifting rarityGrant's WINDOW before the roll (the only position where reduced and increased are symmetric). Signed-integer deltas per kind per rung (OQ1), shifting BOTH min and max (OQ2). unique and boss are two rows with identical values today -- different acquisition routes that will diverge (OQ3). APPEND-ONLY and pinned to catalog_revision exactly like rarityGrant: a post-ship edit re-sockets every item ever dropped. The set row is 0 below fused ON PURPOSE: chaff/sprout are {0,0} and grafted/cultivated sit at min 0, so any -1 there is a load REJECTION (negative window), not a quieter reduction. The unique/boss +1 has no visible effect at sunwoven/almanac until the eight-socket topology lands (derived {3,5} resolves to 4 through the downstream clamps) -- the parser REPORTS those cells in StructuralBoundNotes rather than hiding them. void has no row: no void source exists yet, and an unknown kind is a load rejection, so a void row appears with the void program, not before.

insertTiers.note: count is a SOFT content axis, not a cap: raising it extends the insert ladder and nothing in this module refuses the higher tier -- it is here so a balance pass can extend it in a file rather than a rebuild. upcycleInputPerOutput is the k -> k+1 stack arithmetic (ssot-sockets.md 4.3), the primary drain on the gem inventory. It is a BOUNDED RATIO between two tiers of one thing, not a ceiling on how much a player may earn.

removal.note: ssot-sockets.md 4.7, tiered by INSERT tier. t1-t2 free (the learning tier), t3 costed with the insert surviving, t4 and above destroys the insert. THE ITEM ALWAYS SURVIVES at every tier -- an item can never be permanently ruined by a bad insert, which is what makes it safe to socket mid-campaign gear. Expressed as two thresholds rather than a per-tier list so extending insertTiers.count needs no edit here.

resonance.note: ringOrder is element-hub-ssot.md 8.5's cycle: fire -> ice -> earth -> air -> fire, four adjacent pairs. eclipsePair is the light/dark mutual counter. attunedEffectiveCountBonus applies to PURE only -- the one shape with a count of same-element contributors to raise; Ring and Eclipse are presence tests with no count, and Diversity's count is of DISTINCT elements, where a +1 would invent an element that is not in the item. attunedTierBonus applies to a Strain or Splice, which has no count to raise (spec-sockets.md 6's two-arm table).

strainSplice.note: D20 fixes a Strain or a Splice at exactly 4 ingredients. It is not a free tunable: it decides how much of an item's body a chaff chassis can capture, and it is what makes the per-actor geometric ceiling 2. Changing it is a reviewed content decision, which is why the parser refuses a value above structuralCeiling -- an ingredient count no item can hold would author 102 combinations nothing can ever fire.
